24.definition: A draft is a piece of written work that is not in its final form.
24.example: He was writing his first draft.

24.definition: To gather is to form a group or bring together.
24.example: We will gather the children before the meeting.

24.definition: A hobby is a fun and creative activity people do in their free time.
24.example: She liked to paint as a hobby.

24.definition: An income is the money you earned from work.
24.example: She was saving her income to buy a house.

24.definition: A jet is a fast plane with a big engine.
24.example: Her company owns a private jet.

24.definition: Maximum is the highest amount of anything allowed.
24.example: The maximum driving speed here is 80 km/h.

24.definition: An official thing is approved by someone in authority.
24.example: Her official degree was being transferred.

24.definition: To recommend means to give advice based on experience.
24.example: His doctor will recommend the best medicine for her cough.

24.definition: To refer to something means to mention or call attention to it.
24.example: Mr. Cid referred to the time to show Bill that he was late for class.

24.definition: A remote place is distant or far away.
24.example: He lived in a remote village in the Himalayas.

24.definition: Sleepless describes a time period in which someone does not sleep.
24.example: Jill had a sleepless night because she had so much on her mind.

24.definition: The volume is the total amount of something.
24.example: The volume of cars in the parking lot was steadily increasing.

25.definition: To circulate is to spread something around, especially in a circular way.
25.example: The fan helped to circulate cool air through the room.

25.definition: Consequent means happening because of a different situation.
25.example: Her consequent rash came after she touched the poisonous plant.

25.definition: To derive means to come, or originate, from a thing or place.
25.example: Red's nickname was derived from the color of her hair.

25.definition: To drown is to die from not being able to breathe underwater.
25.example: He would have drowned if the sailors had not rescued him.

25.definition: A dynasty is a series of rulers who are all from the same family.
25.example: The ancient Egyptians had a dynasty that lasted for many years.

25.definition: A fraction is a small part of something.
25.example: Only a fraction of the milk was used.

25.definition: Frost is a white layer of ice that forms during very cold weather.
25.example: In the morning, the trees were all covered with frost.

25.definition: An illusion is something that looks real, but doesn't actually exist.
25.example: Some pictures create an illusion for the eyes.

25.definition: To invade is to take over a place by force.
25.example: The enemy forces tried to invade our country from the sky.

25.definition: A lieutenant is a rank in the military or police, or a person with that rank.
25.example: The lieutenant was a good leader, and his soldiers respected him.

25.definition: Marine describes something related to the sea.
25.example: A healthy ocean is full of marine animals.

25.definition: A merit is a positive or good quality.
25.example: The actor received an award for his merits in the movie.

25.definition: A navy is the part of a country's military that fights at sea.
25.example: My country is known for our strong navy.

25.definition: Polar relates to the cold places on Earth's north and south ends.
25.example: Only a few people live in the Earth's northern polar region.

25.definition: A ray is a line of light that comes from a bright object.
25.example: The sun's warm rays covered the beach.

25.definition: To resign means to quit a job.
25.example: After I officially resigned from work, I said goodbye to my boss.

25.definition: Suicide is the act of killing oneself.
25.example: Some people feel so sad that they think suicide is the only answer.

25.definition: To tremble is to shake as a result of excitement or cold weather.
25.example: Harry was not used to the cold, so he trembled most of the day.

25.definition: An underlying thing is a hidden cause or reason.
25.example: Her underlying fear of flying reduced her traveling options.

25.definition: Via introduces a route or means of travel.
25.example: We arrived in the city from the airport via the train.

26.definition: To alter something means to change it.
26.example: I altered the color of my nails to match my hair.

26.definition: An action done aside is toward the side of something or someplace.
26.example: The man stood aside and opened the door for me.

26.definition: Autumn is the season of the year between summer and winter.
26.example: I love when the leaves fall in autumn because I can play in them.

26.definition: To blend is to mix two or more things together so that they become one thing.
26.example: My wife blended together all of the ingredients to make a delicious stew.

26.definition: To collapse is to fall down suddenly.
26.example: The tree collapsed right in front of our house.

26.definition: To crush something is to press it together so its shape is destroyed.
26.example: Selena's new car was crushed when she fell on top of it.

26.definition: A curve is to move in a line that bends and does not go straight.
26.example: The road curves to the left and to the right.

26.definition: A disgusting thing is very unpleasant.
26.example: After running all day, Greg's feet had a disgusting odor.

26.definition: A drain is a pipe that carries away water from a building, such as in a kitchen.
26.example: The water in the sink goes down the drain as you wash your hands.

26.definition: To embrace is to hug.
26.example: When they saw each other again, the happy couple embraced.

26.definition: To envy someone is to wish that you had something that other person has.
26.example: Sally envied the happy couple.

26.definition: Fireworks are objects that create colored lights when they are lit.
26.example: The display of fireworks was so beautiful.

26.definition: Flour is a powder made from plants that is used to make foods like bread.
26.example: I wanted to bake a pie, but I needed flour.

26.definition: A fuse is a string on fireworks that burns to make them explode.
26.example: The boy lit the fuse on the rocket and waited for it to burst in the sky.

26.definition: Ginger is a root of a plant that is used to make food spicy and sweet.
26.example: Ginger is a common ingredient in many dishes from India.

26.definition: A jealous person might take something from you.
26.example: Miriam was jealous because Sue was paying too much attention to Jim.

26.definition: A paste is a thick and smooth substance.
26.example: My son needed some paste for a school project.

26.definition: A receipt is a paper that proves that something was received or bought.
26.example: After looking at my receipt, I realized that I had spent too much money.

26.definition: To wipe something is to slide a piece of cloth over it to clean it.
26.example: She wiped the dust from the windows.

26.definition: A wire is a thin string made out of metal.
26.example: The wires were connected to towers that brought electricity to the city.

27.definition: To acknowledge something is to accept that it is true or that it exists.
27.example: The teacher acknowledged that the young student was hungry.

27.definition: An ambassador is a government worker who works in another country.
27.example: The ambassador from Korea was in charge of the conference.

27.definition: A blonde is a person with light-colored hair.
27.example: My cousin is a blonde with blue eyes.

27.definition: To conquer a place means to attack and take control of it.
27.example: The soldiers were trying to conquer the world.

27.definition: To drag something means to pull it across the ground.
27.example: The dog was dragging his owner down the street.

27.definition: To exaggerate is to say that something is bigger or better than it really is.
27.example: Jimmy wasn't exaggerating about the seriousness of his injury.

27.definition: Heritage is the collection of features of a society, such as language and religion.
27.example: Teepees are part of the heritage of the Native Americans of the plains.

27.definition: To insult someone is to say things that will hurt the person's feelings.
27.example: The girls insulted each other all afternoon.

27.definition: An action that happens meanwhile happens at the same time as another action.
27.example: He wants to be a doctor in the future, but meanwhile, he works a regular job.

27.definition: A necklace is a piece of jewelry that people wear around their necks.
27.example: Joyce received a lovely pearl necklace for her wedding anniversary.

27.definition: A noble is a rich and powerful person.
27.example: The Queen invited a noble from a nearby country to dinner.

27.definition: A precious thing is valuable and important.
27.example: In a desert, water can be more precious than money.

27.definition: A prejudice is an unfair opinion about people based on the group they belong to.
27.example: The company's rules against gender prejudice must be enforced.

27.definition: A rumor is a story that may not be true.
27.example: Carla was spreading rumors around the office.

27.definition: A sin is something that is wrong for religious reasons.
27.example: Taking something that doesn't belong to you is a sin.

27.definition: A spectacle is an amazing sight.
27.example: Niagara Falls is quite a spectacle.

27.definition: A stack is a pile of different things.
27.example: There was a stack of paperwork on his desk to complete.

27.definition: A suspicious person does not trust others, or is not trusted by others.
27.example: Dad was suspicious of the caller on the line.

27.definition: Tin is an inexpensive metal.
27.example: Soup is a food that is often sold in tin cans.

27.definition: A vase is an attractive container in which people keep flowers.
27.example: The vase was filled with lovely flowers.

28.definition: To ache is to hurt, or cause pain.
28.example: Mindy's head ached because she bumped it against the wall.

28.definition: Arctic shows that something is of or from the cold, far-north part of the Earth.
28.example: It is cold when the arctic winds blow.

28.definition: A canal is a path for water to travel through.
28.example: The city of Venice, Italy, has many canals.

28.definition: A chemist is a scientist who works with chemicals.
28.example: My mother is a successful chemist who helps invent new products.

28.definition: A chill is a feeling of cold.
28.example: The chill from the cold wind made Bill shiver.

28.definition: Congress is a group of leaders in a government.
28.example: Congress makes laws for people to follow.

28.definition: Dairy shows that something is made from milk.
28.example: Things like milk and cheese are dairy foods.

28.definition: To descend is to go downward.
28.example: I descended the stairs to get out of the building.

28.definition: A grocer is a person who sells food.
28.example: Our grocer, Mr. Smith, is a very kind man.

28.definition: To hesitate is to wait for a short time before doing something.
28.example: He hesitated for a moment before he decided which one to choose.

28.definition: An institution is an organization that works to help a city or group of people.
28.example: Banks are vital institutions that businesses and people use every day.

28.definition: To jog is to run slowly.
28.example: He jogs every day so he can be healthier.

28.definition: A merchant is a person who sells things.
28.example: The merchant was selling used cars.

28.definition: To poke something is to push something quickly with your finger or a pointed object.
28.example: I poked my finger on a thumb tack.

28.definition: To postpone something is to make it happen later than planned.
28.example: They postponed the meeting until Elena arrived.

28.definition: To splash is to crash into something so that liquid spreads out.
28.example: Some green paint splashed upon the floor.

28.definition: Stubborn people don't change their minds easily.
28.example: Both of my parents are stubborn. They never give in to each other.

28.definition: A suburb is a small part of a large city.
28.example: I grew up in the suburbs, only a few minutes outside of the city.

28.definition: The tide is the level of the water in the sea.
28.example: The tide continued to crawl upon the beach little by little.

28.definition: A tragedy is a very sad event.
28.example: It was a tragedy when his house was struck by lightning and burned.

29.definition: A bomb is an object that explodes and destroys large areas.
29.example: The bomb will destroy anything that is nearby.

29.definition: A certificate is a document that says that something is true or happened.
29.example: I was given a certificate for completing the computer course.

29.definition: A circumstance is an event that makes a situation what it is.
29.example: There were many circumstances behind their success, like hard work.

29.definition: A coffin is a box used to bury dead people.
29.example: When people pass away, they are usually buried inside of a coffin.

29.definition: To cope with a difficult or stressful situation means to deal with it.
29.example: He copes with work stress by exercising three or four times a week.

29.definition: Criticism is the act of saying that something is not correct or good.
29.example: She had a lot of criticism about their new plan.

29.definition: To devastate something is to cause great damage or pain to that thing.
29.example: The entire wall was devastated.

29.definition: To frown is to make an unhappy look with one's face.
29.example: Melissa frowned when she found out that the party had been cancelled.

29.definition: To gaze at something means to look at it for a long time.
29.example: We used a telescope to gaze at the stars for over an hour.

29.definition: To glance at something means to look at it quickly.
29.example: She glanced behind her to see if he was looking at her.

29.definition: Grief is the feeling of deep sadness, usually when a person dies.
29.example: The grief caused by losing her parents was very difficult for her.

29.definition: A groom is a man who is going to be married.
29.example: The groom looked happy as he walked with his new wife.

29.definition: A license is an official document that gives one permission to do something.
29.example: In the United States, you need a driver's license to drive legally.

29.definition: A microscope is a device that makes small objects look bigger.
29.example: Germs cannot be seen without a microscope.

29.definition: Nuclear things relate to the division or joining of atoms.
29.example: Nuclear power plants provide inexpensive energy to cities.

29.definition: To portray something means to describe it or show it in a picture.
29.example: Her picture portrayed the house she grew up in when she was little.

29.definition: To rotate something means to turn it around in a circle.
29.example: An airplane's propellers rotate quickly to help it fly.

29.definition: A souvenir is something bought to remember of a place or event.
29.example: I bought a Russian doll as a souvenir on my trip to Moscow.

29.definition: A submarine is a boat that can go underwater for long periods of time.
29.example: The submarine dove under the sea so the enemy couldn't see it.

29.definition: To trace something means to follow over it with the eyes or a finger.
29.example: He traced over the graph with his finger.

30.definition: A coastline is the outline of a country's coast.
30.example: He noticed that most of the cities in Australia are on the coastline.

30.definition: To deter means to prevent or discourage someone from doing something.
30.example: Icy roads deter people from driving their cars.

30.definition: To devise something means to come up with an idea or plan about it.
30.example: The thieves devised a plan to steal the diamonds.

30.definition: A distance is how far it is between two points.
30.example: The distance between America and Russia is about 8,000 km.

30.definition: Expertise is the knowledge and skills to do something well.
30.example: John has a lot of advertising expertise. He can sell anything!

30.definition: A fracture is a crack or break in something.
30.example: Don't stand on that leg because there's a fracture. It might get worse.

30.definition: A headache is a pain in one's head.
30.example: My sister gets a headache every time she has a lot of stress.

30.definition: To implement something means to ensure that what has been planned is done.
30.example: The school decided to implement a new teaching strategy.

30.definition: Insight is a deep and accurate understanding of something.
30.example: The physics textbook gave the student a new insight about gravity.

30.definition: A limb is a large branch on a tree.
30.example: The monkey sat on the tree limb and enjoyed a piece of fruit.

30.definition: Might means strength or power.
30.example: Try with all your might to lift the heavy tire.

30.definition: Optimism is the state of being hopeful about the future.
30.example: The mother had optimism about her children's futures.

30.definition: Proficient means able to do something well.
30.example: Secretaries are proficient at typing quickly.

30.definition: A raft is a flat kind of boat.
30.example: He sailed across the Pacific Ocean on a raft.

30.definition: A ridge is a long, narrow piece of raised land.
30.example: The brown bear walked along the edge of the mountain ridge.

30.definition: The shoulder is the body part between the top of the arm and the neck.
30.example: He carried his bike on his shoulder.

30.definition: To shove something is to push it with a lot of power.
30.example: She shoved him out of the way.

30.definition: A spouse is the person to whom someone is married.
30.example: I live in a home with my spouse and two children.

30.definition: To thrust means to push or move something quickly with a lot of force.
30.example: The boxer thrust his fist into the punching bag.

30.definition: To tolerate something means to be able to accept it even when it is unpleasant.
30.example: When you are in a hurry, it can be hard to tolerate traffic signals.
